correctness.rationale: The two equations share the same instantaneous consumption flux \(G(n,p)p\), while predator recruitment receives its delayed copy multiplied by \(e^{- eta	au}\). Integrating a positive periodic solution over one period and shifting the delayed term gives \(\overline{Gp}=e^{ eta	au} ar p\). The prey integral then gives the exact mean law, and the identity \(\overline{n^2}= ar n^2+\operatorname{Var}(n)\) gives the variance form. Fixed positive prey makes the prey-loss function strictly increasing in predator density, so a nonconstant cycle has positive prey variance. The logistic parabola gives the strict mean ceiling. Since \(G<1/h_1\), the integrated predator equation forces \(h_1e^{ eta	au}<1\). The bundled symbolic checker verifies the algebra and monotonicity; no simulation is used as proof.

value.rationale: The source is explicitly about how maturation delay changes oscillatory coexistence and predator extinction. The accepted identity gives a finite-amplitude quantitative law for those oscillations: juvenile mortality contributes the exact factor \(e^{- eta	au}\), prey variability subtracts an exact variance penalty, and every positive cycle obeys a simple handling-time/delay obstruction. This supplies a model-specific diagnostic and parameter ceiling for the recurrent states studied in the paper, rather than a routine restatement of a local linear condition.
